authentication: historically none; the surviving ODP dataset-product path requires X-API-KEY
cost_notes: Free of charge when reachable; the real cost is storage/bandwidth (multi-TB) and engineering time, not licence fees.
free_tier: public domain and free where reachable; currently key-gated through ODP
historical_coverage: grant full text 2001+; pre-grant publications 2001+ (per USPTO documentation)
known_limitations: PROBED 2026-11-09: https://bulkdata.uspto.gov/ does NOT resolve (getaddrinfo failed; the domain returns only an SOA record, and 8.8.8.8 agrees). The long-standing anonymous file tree is retired in this environment.
https://data.uspto.gov/bulkdata returns the ODP SPA shell (HTTP 200, no file listing); the ODP dataset-product API answers 401 (and 403 on the collection endpoint) without X-API-KEY.
ZERO bytes of bulk data were downloaded in this round; the honest status is 'no verified anonymous bulk channel', not 'verified bulk download'.

Historical file sizes are the real blocker even when reachable: one weekly grant ZIP is roughly 100-600 MB and the full back catalogue is multi-TB, so a full ingest is a streaming/bandwidth project rather than an API call.
The same invention appears twice in the corpus (pre-grant publication and grant), so de-duplication must use publication/family numbers, not titles.
There is no query interface: filtering by assignee means downloading and streaming XML locally.
licence: US government work, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105)
rate_limits: no request-rate concept for files; ODP API rate limits apply to its dataset endpoints
research_value: Only worth pursuing if patent full text (abstract/claims/description) is required for many tens of thousands of documents, because there is no query layer and the volume is multi-TB. For assignee/date/title-level linkage the keyed ODP API is cheaper and sufficient; this source is therefore a P1 fallback, not a primary channel.
timestamp_fields: date-publ in the grant/application XML = publication date -> source_public_at
update_frequency: weekly (when the file tree is reachable)
